The committee split on a new health-insurance stabilization transfer and on a new Assistant Town Manager/HR Director grade, and it postponed voting on its recommendation for the Proposition 2½ override so the full five-member board, including two absent members, could weigh in before the mailing deadline.

budget_items.what_was_said: A new revolving fund would let the economic development committee handle sponsorship money for events like the meet-and-greet without it passing through the town's general accounts. FY2027 spending cap discussed.

Spending limits were read for ambulance billing, timber rights, school custodial special details, Green Thumb, library, Council on Aging, storm water task force, electric/gas/plumbing inspector, technology, wetlands protection fees, COA meal site, and parks programming revolving funds.
Two outstanding invoices to Aeroseptic were named as the only known prior-year bills so far; recommendation deferred to town meeting since more may surface.

budget_items.topic: FY26 closeout / snow and ice deficit
budget_items.what_was_said: The current estimated operating deficit, driven mostly by snow and ice removal, was given; transfers will cover part of it and up to a stated amount was earmarked from free cash pending final snow and ice bills.
Two override tiers would go to voters as separate ballot questions, with only the highest approved amount implemented; the Finance Committee deferred taking a position pending the full board.

An accounting error had moved the same unspent FY23 capital funds through two prior votes (TCP roof repair, then FY26 capital); this article unwinds both so the money returns to the FY26 capital plan cleanly.

Individual capital items were read out including DPW bridge completion, a police cruiser, a fire engine/brush truck, primary school entry/driveway and playground design, public safety building roof and boiler work, door security intercoms at Turkey Hill and the primary school, and a DPW front-end loader.
The planned motion would transfer this amount from solid waste enterprise revenue to operate the program for FY2027; the fund does not cover recycling costs.
The fund would use enterprise revenue to pay Fitchburg for water and recoup a percentage under an intermunicipal agreement; figures were based on usage estimates.
A transfer toward the sewer enterprise's share of retiree health benefit liability; a member asked why the PEG/PAC enterprise carries no similar contribution.
Total FY2027 operating budget figure for the sewer enterprise fund.

budget_items.topic: SAP salary schedule / cost of living adjustment
budget_items.what_was_said: A cost-of-living increase for non-union salaried employees would be funded from the salary reserve; a member clarified it is not tied to any federal COLA figure.

budget_items.topic: Special appropriation: TC Pasio and assessor position
budget_items.what_was_said: Funds requested for TC Pasio operating and decommissioning costs and for a special assistant to the assessor position.

budget_items.topic: Free cash to OPEB trust fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Ten percent of certified free cash was described as being transferred to the OPEB trust under the town's financial policy.
A second consecutive year of a small deposit was proposed to build a cushion against retirement buyout costs exceeding the operating budget line.
Funds requested for activities marking the town's 300th anniversary; some members felt the amount was too large given past reliance on volunteers.
A standard annual transfer from free cash to the general-purpose stabilization fund, distinct from the vehicle/special purpose fund.

A new deposit was proposed as a cushion against a future spike in health insurance costs; total town and school insurance costs across active and retiree accounts were estimated. One member asked for defined trigger criteria for using the fund before supporting it.

budget_items.topic: Vacation accrual system transition liability buyout
budget_items.what_was_said: The town proposed buying out the full accrued-vacation liability at current dollar value ahead of a transition to a continuous accrual system, covering SAP employees and settled/near-settled union groups.
A member recalled roughly this figure as the cost of printing and mailing full warrant booklets to every household, cited in favor of switching to a postcard notice.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the mechanics of nearly every vote (motion, outcome, and any split count) once articles are matched up, but they diverge in two ways worth flagging: the official minutes record every dollar figure zero times (they give motion/seconder/roll-call only), so almost none of "ours" many dollar amounts can be checked against them, and there are several real vote-outcome conflicts — Article Q (300th anniversary) is unanimous in the official record but "4-1" in ours, Article P (compensated absence reserve) has a Jay Simeone nay the official record shows but ours omits, and two articles ours marked "not audible" (O, Z2) the official record shows were unanimously approved. A reader should check the actual warrant to resolve which SAP article (N vs. EE) corresponds to the "Assistant Town Manager/HR Director grade" item ours describes, since the two records' SAP-related outcomes don't cleanly line up.

what_happened.line: The committee put off recommending a position on the FY27 Proposition 2½ override until the full five-member board can meet.
It also deferred the FY27 omnibus town and school operating budget because final transfer figures were not yet ready.
A new special-purpose health insurance stabilization fund transfer passed its recommendation on a 4-1 vote.
A proposed Assistant Town Manager/HR Director grade change was pushed to the next meeting after members said it needed further discussion.
Most routine warrant articles -- revolving funds, the FY27 capital budget, and the water and solid waste enterprise funds -- were recommended for approval.

why_it_matters: The override recommendation touches what residents are asked to approve at town meeting or the ballot, and the committee is not yet on record with a position.
The FY27 omnibus budget funds town and school operations for the coming year; its numbers were not final at this meeting.
The health insurance stabilization fund is a new savings mechanism for a cost that affects both town and school budgets, and it did not pass without dissent.
watch_next: The next Finance Committee meeting, when the full board is expected to take up the override recommendation.

budget_items.what_was_said: The general fund free cash was certified this week; Karen Brochu was thanked for putting together the free cash submission to the state.
Bill Bernard presented an overall DPW budget higher than previous years, covering mandatory work, a new part-time clerk, restored pavement management, and MS4 storm water compliance money.

budget_items.topic: Catch basin cleaning and sweeping performance
budget_items.what_was_said: In-house work over the last three years has completed about 30% of catch basin cleaning and 22% of street sweeping, well short of what is mandated.
Bernard estimated it would cost about $100,000 less per year to contract out catch basin cleaning and sweeping than to hire three additional staff.
Bernard modeled a 3% annual increase for DPW, clerical union, and himself across FY25-27 to estimate roughly $52,000 in added salary cost, pending ongoing CBA negotiations.
The snow and ice budget is being increased 2.5% per year to close the gap between budget and actual spending, currently around $800,000.
Vehicle repair costs sent out to contractors exceeded the budgeted line significantly last year, prompting a requested increase.
The recycling budget was reduced after a closer look at actual spending; last year's budget was much higher than what is actually being spent.
The trash program is described as roughly self-funding at about $500,000 per year.
DPW cited a small bridge grant for the Flaill road bridge, a storm water asset management grant from the Mass Clean Water Trust, and a pending Mass Community Cover grant for engineering on a culvert.
Bernard plans to apply for a Complete Streets grant and has a cost estimate of about a million dollars for sidewalk construction and repair between the high school and Marshall Park.
Chapter 90 funding for FY27 is expected at a higher level than the typical amount; continuing at the higher level over several years would add nearly $1.7 million versus normal funding.
The sewer enterprise fund budget is just under $2 million, with expenses and revenues nearly balanced showing an estimated small surplus.
The town pays Leominster and Fitchburg to treat sewage since Lunenburg has no treatment plant of its own; this is the largest driver of the sewer budget.
The engineering line was budgeted at $30,000 last year but actual cost was $80,000 after DEP required additional engineering work; the line is being increased again.
Money is set aside to replace aging pumps, controllers, and pipe as the sewer system approaches the end of its design life.

Without a rate increase, user charge revenue was estimated to leave a large deficit; with the proposed rate increase the budget shows only a small surplus, avoiding further draws on retained earnings.
The proposed sewer rate increase is about 16%, driven by Leominster and Fitchburg raising their own disposal charges.

The per-unit user rate would rise from its current level to a higher figure (about 16% increase), while the minimum charge rises only about 5%, intended to soften the impact on lower-usage households.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager's budget rose substantially to fund a new assistant town manager position for a full year; restructuring by eliminating the communications/IT director position reduced the net new cost from $120,000 to $60,000.
Audit costs are rising because the town's former auditing firm was absorbed into a larger firm (CBIZ) at greater cost, and a competing firm lacked capacity to take on the town.
Small reductions were made to the treasurer and collector office budgets based on actual spending, including contracted services covering the deputy tax collector and Unibank services.

FY26 and FY25 real estate exemption counts and total dollar amounts were compared; the senior means-tested exemption was not approved for FY2025.

The town report/printing line rose sharply because it had not been properly budgeted, covering the annual report, town meeting booklet, and special town meeting warrant printing and mailing.
The reserve fund is level funded; the town manager raised the idea of increasing it given department budgets are being tightened, citing prior years' transfer amounts.
The salary reserve has not been adjusted for FY27 pending outcomes of ongoing DPW, clerical, and firefighter contract negotiations; an anticipated 3% COLA for non-union (SAP) employees is assumed.
Central purchasing, which now includes consolidated postage costs, is level funded.
The veterans budget is largely driven by Chapter 115 benefit payments currently serving seven residents; the town receives trailing state reimbursement the following fiscal year.
This line rose almost entirely due to the non-discretionary Worcester County retirement assessment.
The unclassified budget, covering liability, workers comp, health, life insurance, unemployment and Medicare, increased from the preliminary figure due to a correction in Medicare supplement counts.

meetings.headline: Finance Committee warns a large school 'restoration' override could fail, as one did in 2012.
meetings.summary: The committee heard FY27 budget presentations from the Council on Aging (level-funded), the Library (a modest increase plus a push for above-level programming funding), and Public Access Cable, which described a widening deficit from declining Comcast franchise fees and a forced studio relocation. The bulk of the meeting was a debate over the upcoming Proposition 2½ override: members worried that bundling the town's mostly level-service requests with the school committee's much larger 'restoration' budget into a single ask risks a failure like the town's 2012 override, which passed by roughly two-to-one against and led to a decade of cuts.

meetings.headline: Town Manager unveiled a preliminary FY27 budget that does not balance without a property tax override
meetings.summary: The Finance Committee heard FY27 budget presentations from the fire, facilities and police departments, each citing staffing, contract and equipment cost drivers, including a fire department fourth-shift staffing proposal and a police restructuring from two school resource officers to one SRO plus a second detective. The Town Manager then presented a preliminary town-wide FY27 budget that she said does not balance and currently relies on a Proposition 2½ override, walking the committee through revenue sources and expenditure categories in detail; no votes were taken on the budget or the override. She also reported that FY25 books were closed out late, risking a hold on state aid, though the town secured a filing extension.

budget_items.topic: Fire Dept total FY27 budget request
budget_items.what_was_said: The chief presented the total fire/EMS budget request, noting a typo, and said it represents about a 22% increase driven mostly by the fourth shift proposal.
The chief said nearly all of the fire budget increase is the fourth shift except for a smaller remaining amount.
Radio maintenance is proposed to rise because portable radio costs have skyrocketed.
Vehicle maintenance is increasing; the chief cited an ambulance with major repair costs and ongoing truck issues.
A requested increase covers farming out vehicle repairs the highway garage can't perform.
The emergency management line, mostly supplies, is unchanged.
The department typically receives a state grant for fire safety and senior safety education.
A multi-year firefighter safety grant, believed ended, reappeared this year and is being spent down.
This federal-through-state grant has not materialized this year amid federal funding disruptions.
The department typically receives donated funds for equipment not covered by the town budget.
One-time mitigation funds are being used for added predium staffing in FY26 and paramedic training in FY27; the chief cautioned these are non-recurring.
The department currently budgets a set number of weekly predium hours, concentrated on Sundays.
Sunday shift predium coverage for three people was quantified in the Q&A on staffing.
A stipend line funds on-call officer coverage on Sundays; it would go away with full career staffing.
The utilities budget rises largely because the TCP building's utility costs are finally being captured in the budget.
The town is adjusting how solar credits are allocated across buildings after accumulating a large surplus that can't be directly applied elsewhere.
The facilities maintenance budget is presented as roughly level service with targeted increases for repairs and contracted maintenance.
A mandated 20-year sprinkler head inspection found failures at the fire department requiring replacement, below the capital threshold.
The town's betterment cost for sewer installation expires after FY28, freeing budget room afterward.
The parks budget rises mainly due to purchase-of-service costs for landscaping and repairs.
The current landscaping contract doesn't cover enough mowing cuts for baseball season and would need additional funding to meet the needed frequency.
The revolving fund collects rent from public access TV and the Shapiro school leasing classrooms, offsetting TCP building costs.

A prior-year capital appropriation for the TCP roof was found to be double-counted with FY26 capital funding for town hall windows/HVAC design; a cleanup warrant article will rescind the original vote.
The police budget is mostly personnel costs driven by the collective bargaining agreement, stipends, overtime and training.

budget_items.topic: Police body armor and software costs
budget_items.what_was_said: Increases fund contractually required 5-year body armor replacement for six officers and new building-access software.
Hospital charges for new-hire physicals, psychological exams and drug tests have risen sharply, shared between police and fire budgets.
Vehicle maintenance is level-funded based on recent years' actuals, aided by cycling in two new cruisers annually.
The lockup line dropped substantially after the town began sending most male prisoners to the Worcester County Sheriff instead of holding them locally.
A state grant funds a co-response mental health clinician shared with Lancaster, which had been lost and then restored.
The department was not awarded its usual highway traffic safety grant this year, which normally funds radar units.
Comfort dog handling fees are a separate cost per dog; an unused second comfort dog would add another handling fee if utilized.
The Town Manager said the preliminary FY27 budget as presented is not balanced and relies on an override of this size, which she expects to keep changing.
Property tax, state aid, local receipts and enterprise funds were broken out as shares of total FY27 revenue.
Enterprise fund revenue is still being finalized pending sewer and PACK enterprise indirect cost work.

meetings.summary: The Finance Committee heard that the town's actual FY27 health insurance increase came in at 8.85% (down from over 20% after eliminating GLP-1 weight-loss drug coverage), and that a level-service town/school budget is unlikely to be balanced without an override. Members discussed how DPW, police, fire and school budgets will be presented in coming weeks, agreed to formally request the school department align its FY27 budget presentation with prior years and show FTEs and a consolidated athletics budget, and began a recurring discussion of how to structure a possible Proposition 2½ override, including the risk of needing another one next year. A committee member recalled that in a past budget year an extra $140,000 was paid toward transportation because it was being counted against the athletics revolving account, cited as a reason to want a consolidated athletics budget.
The chair explained that the level-service budget the committee will hear is likely not a balanced budget, and above-level-service or restorative requests will also be presented separately.

The chair described three possible budget scenarios the committee is dealing with: level service (likely requiring an override), increased/restorative service (a larger override), or a balanced budget reached through cuts.

The finance director said the level-service budget she is presenting already includes some cuts regardless of the override outcome, citing as an example a reduction from 5 days a week to 4 days a week of an unspecified service.

A member asked that the school present one consolidated athletics budget including expenses paid from the revolving account, a practice she said stopped around 2020.
The committee agreed to formally request that the FY27 school budget be presented in the same format as FY26 and FY25, clearly showing level service versus extra items and FTE per salary line.
A member raised concern that the Capital Planning Committee is reviewing a turf field replacement project that was never a ranked priority submitted by the school department, questioning the process.

The chair warned there is a high likelihood that even a level-service override passed this year could be followed by another level-service override next year, and floated setting the levy limit higher than taxed in year one to build headroom.

decisions.decision: DPW, police, and fire/facilities budgets are judged firm enough to present next week even though some union contracts (e.g., DPW Teamsters) are not yet finalized.

Lunenburg's FY27 assessment to Monty Tech would rise mainly because of the state's minimum contribution formula, not Monty Tech's own spending growth.

meetings.headline: FinCom says FY27 leaves almost no room after health insurance; a school override looms and deep cuts are floated
meetings.summary: The Finance Committee heard that the finance/accounting office is in crisis (a departed finance director, an unclosed FY25, a retired accountant filling in part-time) and got an early FY27 revenue estimate that leaves very little after health insurance. Members debated whether to support another Proposition 2½ override, with one member insisting the town do "hard work" on cuts (recycling, the TCP building, ambulance receipts, capital funding sources) before any override is considered, while the town manager warned that a no-override budget likely means real staffing/service cuts. The committee also adjusted its budget-season calendar to bring Monty Tech and the schools in earlier, reviewed the capital plan ranking, water billing/enterprise fund problems, and approved its prior minutes and adjournment by roll call.
